environment: Claude Code cloud container, Linux, Python 3.11.16 (project venv) plus a separate sympy 1.13.3 review venv; main 7a2d233
method: symbolic offset-curve dkappa/dl for general k(s), t(s) (sympy), compared with the reviewed closed form
symbolic truncated-power identity and end-condition minors
hand re-derivation of every interval enclosure (c0, w, w/c0, B-spline derivative bounds, endpoint bounds, nonlinear r^d bound)
dense numeric baseline monotonicity, knot-simplex grid of both linear coefficients, nonlinear excess grid
exact rational coefficients at all five simplex vertices and equal spans
end-to-end: 768 real candidate XMLs (reviewer's own Cox-de Boor basis and record splitting) judged by the unmodified production local_shape.compare
rerun of the reviewed research.py in a fresh directory

findings.road10_reference_on_domain: one spiral covers [a, b] in the exact decimal model (end 89.2662981386559 >= b); laneOffset and right -1/-2 widths are affine with no record inside (a, b)

linear_coefficient_check.remark: the uniform bound holds but is tight to 0.2% at this simplex vertex, where B1''' equals the enclosure's lower end

end_to_end.observation: every u,v>=0 sample inside the endpoint cap regresses the lane -2 rate in the cell starting at the witness station; lane -2/-1 centre and edges and curvature peaks regress as well, so the actual checker rejects more than the proof needs

findings.fewer_spans: agree: four spans leave one B-spline whose two endpoint conditions force opposite signs, so zero; three or fewer spans have dimension <= 0
findings.reference_linkage: agree: fixed left world edges and positive width at the same s fix the reference normal, hence tangent and (with a fixed start) the reference line

remarks: derivation.json was produced by an earlier research.py: a rerun adds the source_proof field (216 source hashes); all mathematical fields are identical; the original file is CRLF
README.md references next-contract-requirements.json, which does not exist; the four requirements live only in the README text

in binary64 the domain start a lies about 1e-15 m inside the previous spiral (a is exactly a primitive boundary in decimal) and the next primitive starts 1e-13 m before the domain spiral ends; outside the stated decimal model, no effect on the exclusion
implementation_recommendation: Do not implement the nonuniform five-span paired laneOffset/median family on this domain. A next tool needs a different, source-backed physical scope (see the reviewed README's four requirements), not a relaxed threshold.
limitations: grids and sampled candidates are evidence; continuum coverage rests on the reviewed interval enclosure, whose formulas were re-derived here
same predeclared domain, fixed reference and paired expression only; no claim about other domains, representations or road 10 in general
the comparison contract itself (domain and cells) was taken as given
